note: Per-piece intent. A brief overrides the general rubric where it says so (e.g. the café is deliberately math rock in 7/8). Keyed by the render file name prefix.
winter: Winter region exploration music ('First Snow at the Station'), 96 BPM, D major, ~30 s seamless loop. Layer L3 = full band (Thriving region); L0 = only pad + bell (Dormant). Should feel snowy, warm and wistful; it plays for long stretches behind gameplay.
green: Green-season region exploration music ('Paddles on Lake Aoki'), 108 BPM, A major, ~27 s seamless loop. Brighter, jangly, outdoorsy summer counterpart to the winter loop. Layer L3 = full band; L0 = pad + bell only.
cafe: Café / kitchen shift music ('Golden Hour at the Hatch'): the player serves customers for ~75 s. Target style for THIS piece (the game owner's choice, overrides the rubric's rock-guitar assumptions): bright Japanese indie funk-pop with a little soul, in the world of muque's 'ブルーライト' — 120 BPM, straight 16ths, four-on-the-floor kick with a dry backbeat, offbeat clean-guitar chanks, staccato bass with pickups, soulful electric-piano comping, warm city-pop 7th/sus harmony, an off-beat lead hook with pockets. Electric piano and four-on-the-floor are CORRECT here. It must feel FUN, bouncy and relaxed, never busy, messy or panicky; space and staccato over density. Bars 13-16 are a deliberate breather. In game the layers build across the shift (L0 keys + guitar, L1 + bass/kick/hats, L2 + snare/16th hats/second guitar, L3 + lead).
